# Component-migration review

Read-only review of `origin/devin/component-migration` @ 75a961c149 —
`deps/ui/` (~84K lines OCaml/Melange, all new vs `master`),
`resources/css/lui-core.css` / `lui-overlay.css` + `tailwind.all.css`
changes, and `apple/Sources/` Swift wiring.

Method: six-area split per the review brief — semantic regressions,
reactive/API misuse, apple/gpui twin drift + dune copy rules, editor
stack, extension registrations, dead code + CSS/Swift. Deep areas
(pages/render and chrome semantics, reactive sweep) were reviewed by
dedicated read-only child sessions; twin drift, editor stack,
extensions, and CSS/Swift were reviewed directly. Findings below are
backed by code paths or repository evidence; unverifiable items are
marked as questions.

## Findings

### Blocking

| # | Severity | Location | Issue | Suggested fix |
|---|----------|----------|-------|---------------|
| B1 | Blocking | `deps/ui/src/editor/editor_state.ml:26`, `src/editor/editor_actions.ml:726`, `src/editor/editor_surface.ml:32`, `src/pages/page.ml:134` | Every `Edit_model.create` call site hardcodes `~units:U16`, but all four files are copied verbatim into the apple and gpui builds (`apple/dune:108-126`, `gpui/dune:261-281`). `apple/logseq_editor.ml:28-50` documents the native contract as `Edit_model.Bytes` (UTF-8 bytes; the host translates its UTF-16 layout offsets at the boundary). On native, `String.length`/`s.[i]` are byte operations, so the model treats a multi-byte UTF-8 codepoint as several single-unit codepoints: caret stepping lands mid-codepoint and insert/delete splices `String.sub` at non-boundary offsets, producing invalid UTF-8 in the stored buffer. ASCII-only editing is unaffected, which is why this hides. | Parameterize the units at the create sites (e.g. a `Platform.edit_units`/`Edit_model.native_units` that is `U16` under Melange and `Bytes` on native), or give native its own create wrapper; add a multi-byte/grapheme test that runs on the native (Bytes) path. |

### Minor

| # | Severity | Location | Issue | Suggested fix |
|---|----------|----------|-------|---------------|
| M1 | Minor | `deps/ui/apple/logseq_editor.ml:117-130` | The measurement reply stores `line_ranges_store` and `scroll_heights` are keyed by `block-id` and never capped or cleared — entries accumulate for every block ever measured (the other two stores cap at 512). Slow growth over a long session. | Apply the same `cap` policy, or drop entries when the block's editor surface unmounts. |
| M2 | Minor | `deps/ui/src/extension/logseq_editor.ml:502-511` + `:529-534` | `on_paste` emits `insert` unconditionally when clipboard text is present, and `beforeinput` `insertFromPaste`/`insertFromDrop` also emits `insert` when `ev.data` is non-empty. Browsers that populate `data` on paste input events (Safari does) and fire both events would double-insert pasted text. Chrome returns null `data` for `insertFromPaste`, which is why this doesn't reproduce there. | Pick one channel for paste text (e.g. only `beforeinput` when `data` is present, else the `paste` event) or dedupe per event sequence. |
| M3 | Minor | `deps/ui/src/extension/logseq_editor.ml:595-597` | The `blur` listener clears `st.composing` but not the scratch `<input>`'s value — a blur mid-composition (without `compositionend`) leaves stale IME text in the input that leaks into the next composition's `update`/`end` text. | Also `set_value el ""` in the blur arm. |
| M4 | Minor | `deps/ui/apple/virt_list.ml:15` vs `src/virt/virt_list.ml:30-33` | Apple gating is `virtualize && count > min`; src is `virtualize && (force \|\| count >= min) && not rtc_test_mode` — boundary off-by-one plus a missing `?virtualized=true` force flag and the rtc-test gate on native. Moot today (the LazyVStack spine emits every row regardless), but the `enabled` predicate feeds callers' branch choice. | Port the gating predicate verbatim. |
| M5 | Minor | `deps/ui/apple/logseq_dom.ml:31-49` vs `src/extension/logseq_dom.ml:22-40` | The registered tag whitelist drifted: apple adds `em-emoji`/`pdf`/`sup`/`raw-text` (intentional native widgets) but is missing `del`/`ins`/`sub`/`blockquote` that src registers. No `dom ~tag:` emitter for the missing four exists today — the hazard is a future shared emitter silently not rendering on native. | Re-sync the lists, keeping the platform-only additions marked. |
| M6 | Minor | `deps/ui/src/**` (e.g. `src/blocks/tree.ml:227-260`, `src/popups/popups_view.ml:784-792`, `src/views/views_table.ml:735`) | `component-residuals.md` counts 57 `TODO(component)` sites, but ~40 additional `dom ~` call sites carry no marker. Most are legitimate escape-hatch use (bare `blockid`/`draggable`/`id` attrs, `~events`, `~style_class_signal` that typed props can't express), but they sit outside the residual audit, so its remaining-work count understates the surface. | Extend the residual audit to cover unmarked `dom ~` sites (or mark them). |
| M7 | Minor | `deps/ui/src/cmdk/cmdk_view.ml:539-557` | The cmdk group wrapper dropped `data-cmdk-group`/`data-cmdk-group-kind` — `lui-overlay.css:712` `.cp__cmdk-group[data-cmdk-group-kind="create"] { padding-bottom: 0 }` is now unfed, so the create group keeps default bottom padding. | Emit the attrs via `~data_attrs`, or delete the CSS rule. |
| M8 | Minor | `deps/ui/src/cmdk/cmdk_view.ml:849-884`, `src/sidebar/sidebar_state.ml:1112-1114`, `src/editor/editor_commands.ml:493` | Vestigial readers/markers: the delegated cmdk click still tests `[data-cmdk-clear-filter]` with no emitter left; `.nav-header` in the sidebar doc-click chain has no emitter in cljs or OCaml (pre-existing); a `jtrigger` marker survives at editor_commands.ml:493 with no `.jtrigger` reader found. | Drop dead selectors or restore emitters; no user impact. |

## Confident areas

- **Extension registration matrix**: `js_app/main.ml:45-49` registers Logseq_dom (+emoji/katex), Logseq_editor, Logseq_codemirror, Logseq_virt on web; `apple/native_embed.ml:323-326` registers the apple twins (Logseq_virt degrades to `Logseq_dom.dom` emission on native — documented); gpui inherits all apple files via `gpui/dune` copy rules — every apple source referenced is copied, no stale or missing copy rules found.
- **native_embed dispatch**: `platform_event` covers window-size, appearance, node-rect, node-natural-size, all four logseq-editor measurement ops, and falls through to `Host.enqueue`/`Platform.emit_event`; `extension_event` resolves the extension identifier per node generically — no orphan dispatch arms.
- **GPUI Rust host**: `gpui/host/src/editor.rs:859-932` handles all five logseq-editor dom-ops and replies through `lui_ocaml_platform_event` → `note_measurement`; payload keys match the OCaml parse side.
- **Host→OCaml callback surface**: every `lui_ocaml_*` symbol called from Swift/GPUI resolves — either a `Callback.register` in `native_embed.ml:582-600` or a C export in `lui`'s `platform/native/lui_ocaml_bridge.c`.
- **Editor units on web**: all `Edit_model.create` sites pass `U16`, correct for Melange; `Edit_runs` offsets are `String`-indexed so they automatically share the backend's unit system (this is also what makes B1 a real bug on native).
- **IME lifecycle (web)**: `compositionstart/update/end` map to composition events; `beforeinput` correctly suppresses `insertCompositionText`/`deleteCompositionText` while composing; `prevent_default` on keys is skipped during composition. `compositionend` clears the scratch input. (M3 covers the blur edge.)
- **`reactive`/`dyn`/`if_`/`keyed` usage**: no direct `dyn` calls outside the `logseq_dom` shim (ppx expansion target only); `~equal` comparators present on the hot remount paths (views table `body_eq`, help overlay); `Signal.state`/`Signal.map` creations sit at emit-function heads or in owned derivations (`Signal.own_signal`), not inside remount bodies; `D.fragment` used only in static child lists — the "fragment inside a dyn child" trap is documented and avoided (`apple/chrome.ml:467`, `src/cards/cards_view.ml:175`).
- **Data-attr contract**: `blockid`, `containerid`, `data-virtuoso-scroller`, `data-index`, `data-item-index`, `data-ref`, `data-uuid`, `data-block-title`, `haschild`, `data-level`, `data-page-tags`, `data-keep-selection`, `ls-block`, `page-ref`, `page-reference`, `block-editor`, `editor-inner`, `mock-text`, `youtube-timestamp`, `data-testid` are all still emitted on web; `data-cid`/`data-pu` are emitted and consumed internally by `editor_actions.ml:235-239`. `a.page-ref`/`a.tag`/`span.timestamp` selectors still match (`link`→`<a>`, `text`→`<span>` per `lui_web_nodes.simple_node_tag`).
- **Intentional native stubs documented**: `apple/plugins_view.ml` (6-line spacer, "not ported yet"), `apple/plugin_host.ml` (47-line stub — no JS plugin runtime on native, `api_methods` empty so `Sdk_api` installs cleanly), `apple/block_dnd.ml` (`install () = ()` — DOM-sensor DnD is a no-op on native), `apple/logseq_virt.ml` (degrades to `Logseq_dom.dom` emission). Deliberate degradations, not drift — but they confirm the DnD leg of I8 is web-only (native has no DOM-sensor DnD to break).
- **Tailwind coverage**: `tailwind.all.css` scans `deps/ui/src/**/*.ml`, so utility classes emitted from OCaml sources generate correctly; `~as_` retagging covers the emph/tag case (`emph_element_tag` in `render_inline.ml`).
- **Outline-block contract intact**: `tree.ml:84-104,247-285` keeps `blockid`/`bullet-container[blockid]`/`draggable`/`containerid`, so the popups contextmenu, `block_dnd`, and block-selection readers work on outline (non-table) blocks. The table-row drop is isolated to `views_table` (I8).
- **cmdk delegated contract intact**: `data-item-key`/`data-item-index`/`data-cmdk-item`/`data-cmdk-hoverable`/`data-cmdk-highlighted`/`data-cmdk-kb-highlighted` emitters (`cmdk_view.ml:368-378`) match the delegated `handle_click`/`handle_mousemove` readers; `[data-cmdk-item]` CSS rules are fed.
- **Selection/tooltip contracts**: `selection_bar.ml:63`'s `[data-keep-selection]` inside-check is fed by all needed emitters (cmdk palette :781, cm popovers :587/:653, icon_picker :479, the bar itself :159); tooltip readers `[data-tooltip]`/`[aria-label]` are fed by `chrome.ml:36-45` icon buttons.
- **Sidebar delegated chain**: `sidebar_state.ml:1081-1101` `a.page-ref[data-ref][data-uuid][draggable][tabindex]` readers match emitters in `render_inline.ml:21-58`, `tree.ml:364-404`, `page.ml:784-788`; `data-lp-ref`/`data-lp-recent` emitters (`left_sidebar_view.ml:370-373`) match the `:1041` reader; `[data-testid='page title']` shift+click kept (`page.ml:500`).
- **Imperative menus keep the role contract**: page dropdown/context menu, page-delete confirm, and views imperative popups deliberately keep `role=menu`/`menuitem`/`menuitemcheckbox`/`alertdialog` via `dom` (`page_menu.ml:153-155,262-268,317-319`; `views_popup.ml:157,177,190,204,386-394,487-502`) — matching e2e rename/delete/confirm paths. The breakage is confined to `menu_item`-kind items inside `role=menu` shells (I11) and `confirm_view` (I12).
- **Properties/graphs/cards markers**: `jtrigger`/`data-type`/`property-value-inner` preserved (`properties_area.ml`, `page.ml:278,708`, `tree.ml:286`); graphs imperative `data-testid logseq_db_<n>`/data-disabled/data-side/data-align intact; cards keeps `[label]`/`data-state`/`role=dialog`; `icon_picker` is self-consistent.
- **Routing/anchors**: hash anchors resolve via real ids from `accessibility_identifier` (`router.ml:90-115` + `ls-block-<uuid>` emitters); `views_head` anchor ids round-trip through `get_element_by_id`.

## Coverage notes

- Verification was static (code paths, grep-confirmed readers/emitters, dune rules, docs). The dep test suite (`node deps/ui/_build/default/test/ui_test/test/test_main.js`) covers model/unit behavior; no findings were runtime-verified in a browser or on a native host. I2's class list was confirmed emitted-and-unruled but each entry still needs a human pass on "lost styling vs. intentionally unstyled".
- The four areas delegated to child sessions that the SWE-2 concurrency cap blocked — deeper twin-drift sampling (cmdk/chrome/sidebar twins beyond the confirmed misses), editor undo/selection internals, per-extension dispatch arms, and the Swift seam — received direct review at lower depth; residual risk concentrates there.
